scenes.justification: hook topology opening with dialogue on why commercial enterprises hedge without seeking speculative profits.

beats.visualIntent: Commercial enterprises trading millions in futures contracts questioning delivery, trading profits, and capital allocation.
Daily operational machinery of margin accounts contrasted with neutralizing commercial price risks to safeguard enterprise solvency.
Variance minimization objective stabilizing corporate cash flows, revenues, and raw material input costs against market price swings.
Two core hedging categories: Short Hedge protecting inventory from falling prices, and Long Hedge locking in raw material costs.

scenes.justification: tension topology contrasting physical commodity inventory risk against short futures contract hedging.

beats.visualIntent: Short Hedge side showing producer with physical commodity production taking short futures contracts against price decline.
Oil producer setup on May 15 with 1M barrels of crude oil, $80 spot price, and $79 August NYMEX futures contract.
Sizing the short hedge by selling exactly 1,000 August NYMEX contracts to cover 1,000,000 barrels at 1,000 barrels per contract.
Spot crash to $75 yielding $75M physical sale plus $4M futures gain, locking in $79M net revenue ($79/bbl effective selling price).

scenes.justification: pillars topology revealing the four foundational pillars of corporate hedging sequentially.

beats.visualIntent: Reveal Pillar 1 (Long Hedge Protection) and Pillar 2 (Price Surge Defense) capping raw material purchase costs against market surges.
Reveal Pillar 3 (Copper Fabricator Setup) showing 100,000 lbs copper needed May 15 at $3.40 spot and $3.20 May COMEX futures.
Reveal Pillar 4 (Net Cost Lockout) with 4 contracts, $325,000 spot outlay offset by $5,000 futures gain to lock in $320,000 net ($3.20/lb).

scenes.justification: formula topology breaking down the symmetrical positions of short vs long hedgers and introducing basis divergence.

beats.visualIntent: Short Hedger natural long exposure with physical inventory offset by short futures position.
Long Hedger natural short liability hedged with long futures position, moving in exact opposite directions.
Breakdown of real-world corporate hedging showing imperfect divergence and introducing Basis Risk.

scenes.justification: process topology tracing the step-by-step causal mechanism from exposure to solvency preservation.

beats.visualIntent: Node 1 (Inception Exposure): Defining basis formula b = S - F as Spot Price S minus Futures Price F.
Node 2 (Market Shock & Basis Divergence): Basis convergence to zero at maturity disrupted by early closeout and grade differences.
Nodes 3 & 4 (Offsetting Cash Flow & Deterministic Revenue): Equations b1 = S1 - F1, b2 = S2 - F2, and short hedger net price Net = F1 + b2.
Node 5 (Solvency Preserved): Replacing outright spot price volatility with smaller basis volatility to compress enterprise risk.

scenes.justification: worked_example topology walking through the mathematical steps of basis strengthening and weakening payoffs.

beats.visualIntent: Givens panel introducing strengthening and weakening basis dynamics for crude oil short hedge parameters.
Calculation step showing basis increase (strengthening) raising short hedger net realized price Net = F1 + b2.
Summary result showing basis decrease (weakening) lowering long hedger net acquisition price for raw materials.

scenes.justification: comparison topology contrasting academic CAPM theory against corporate variance reduction reality.

beats.visualIntent: Left side introducing CAPM theoretical skepticism questioning corporate commodity hedging.
Left trap details: diversified shareholders eliminate unsystematic risk, rendering corporate hedging redundant.
Right reality & verdict: bankruptcy distress costs, debt covenants, and credit ratings justify corporate variance reduction.

scenes.justification: table topology comparing directional basis outcomes and real-world executive dilemma snapshots.

beats.visualIntent: Table row 1: The Worse Outcome Dilemma with crude oil at $80 rallying to $120 causing massive futures margin calls.
Table row 2: Management evaluating derivatives in isolation losing $40/bbl despite physical business record profit.
Table row 3: American Barrick gold mining case buying back hedges at billions in losses during 2000s bull market.

scenes.justification: quantity_over_time topology tracking the sequential delivery month rules and illiquidity metrics.

beats.visualIntent: Counter setup highlighting 2 critical strategic decisions: contract selection and optimal Delivery Month.
Golden rule metric: select delivery month strictly later than closeout date (May sale hedges with June contract).
Risk counter: delivery month liquidity dries up with erratic price swings and unexpected delivery notice liabilities.

scenes.justification: quiz topology prompting active recall of net realized price calculations under basis divergence.

beats.visualIntent: Question display: oil producer with F1 = $90/bbl, August S2 = $85/bbl, F2 = $87/bbl asking for net realized price per barrel.
Thinking timer interval reminding physical sale $85 and short futures gain from 90 to 87 to find terminal basis b2.
Reveal Option B ($88/bbl) with full math: b2 = 85 - 87 = -$2, Net = 90 + (-$2) = $88/bbl (physical $85 + $3 futures gain).

scenes.justification: wisdom topology synthesizing risk transformation into basis risk and charting the bridge to Part 2.

beats.visualIntent: Left panel showing risk transformation: outright price volatility replaced by manageable Basis Risk.
Right panel preview: Cross Hedging jet fuel with heating oil, Minimum Variance Hedge Ratio, and $1.3B Metallgesellschaft collapse.

scenes.justification: summary topology codifying the eight foundational rules of corporate hedging.

beats.visualIntent: Summary thread overview introducing the four structural pillars of corporate hedging.
Pillar 1 cards: Short hedge locking in inventory selling prices and Long hedge capping raw material acquisition costs.
Pillar 2 cards: Basis defined as b = S - F substituting spot price volatility with manageable basis risk.
Pillar 3 cards: Strengthening basis raising short hedger proceeds and weakening basis lowering long hedger costs.
Pillar 4 cards: Delivery month maturing strictly after hedge closeout to avoid illiquidity and delivery notices.
Closing synthesis card previewing Minimum Variance Hedge Ratio, beta hedging, and Metallgesellschaft rollover disaster.
